Title: The Dying Arrivals

In the twilight realm where the souls of all who've passed beyond lived and waited upon return, the world stretched out like an endless expanse. This place was as vast as the soul itself—a sea without end, waves crashing against the unceasing silence. A figure stumbled from her own body, floating aimlessly at the bottom of the abyss.

"My God," she whispered to herself, her voice carried along with the breeze. She was alone, lost among the countless entities who had journeyed here before her. Fear gripped her heart, squeezing it dry, but she forced herself to breathe deeply. Each breath brought more air into her lungs, pushing back at the weight in her chest.

She floated forward until her eyes settled upon the most familiar shape—her own reflection. Her eyes widened in recognition and then narrowed as she stared at the face reflected before her—the ghostly image of a young woman named Margaret.

"You're... you're Margaret?" she stammered, unable to look away. It wasn't right; she knew this woman existed, yet now she stood beside her grave, not alive, merely memory incarnate.

Another consciousness appeared before them both, floating down towards them slowly, hesitant. As they came closer, his name floated between them—they called him Robert.

"A friend from the past..." he said, a tremble in his tone. He stepped towards her, reaching out a hand hesitantly. She reached up to take his, surprised by how fragile it felt.

As they held hands, they felt the connection, a bond made through death's touch. Their eyes met again, meeting each other in silence, then shared a momentary smile. There was relief here, sorrow mixed with hope for a future together.

They watched as others approached the shore, some laughing, some crying, but none looked back. All they could do was continue on together, finding solace in each other's arms.
